correctness.rationale: The nilpotent normalized child shift is generationwise isometric; the orthogonal difference spaces W_d give mutually orthogonal forward chains of exact multiplicity (b-1)b^{d-1}. Diagonalizing (I-J)^*(I-J) on each chain yields the exact sine singular multiset. Chain proportions converge geometrically and have exponentially decaying truncation errors even after fixed polynomial moment weighting. The first singular value gives the sharp exponential tail; the special angle pi/6 yields the atom at one, and row sums prove the exact HS identity. All quantifiers and boundaries, including h=0, b>=2, p>=0, were checked; finite numerical tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Direct comparisons distinguish this height-growing discrete vertex-tree singular law from previously proved fixed metric-tree approximation number asymptotics, Wold shift decompositions, known single-chain sine spectra and leaf-only ancestral matrices. Prior ingredients are credited; the claimed contribution is their branching-weighted global limiting distribution, support, sharp tail, moment and special-atom consequences. No covering prior statement was found in the inspected full text and public research search results. Unindexed equivalents remain a bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A prior paper may have an equivalent finite homogeneous-tree resolvent decomposition and implicit empirical spectral limit under different terminology; absence of a search hit does not prove priority.
The Wold-type branching decomposition and one-chain sine spectrum are previously understood and are explicitly excluded from stand-alone novelty claims.
Publicly indexed paper comparisons and accessible mathematical full texts were checked, but no independent exhaustive bibliography audit has been done.

value.rationale: The all-singular-value empirical distribution on exponentially growing homogeneous trees is a natural invariant of the discrete Hardy ancestor operator. The limit is a dense pure-point law with an exact exponential spectral upper tail, a nontrivial atom, explicit moments, and a logarithmically diverging extremal singular value despite finite quadratic average. This describes how branching shifts spectral mass across chain lengths, a phenomenon beyond a single-block textbook computation and an informative benchmark for extensions to other tree kernels.
